messages.content: Hi, I'm Hua. I've been planning to take the high-speed rail from Beijing to Lhasa next month. Have you heard about that route?
Hello, Hua! Yes, it's a fantastic journey. The train goes through Qinghai and arrives in Lhasa. It's very popular since the service improved a few years ago. What time do you want to leave?
Well, I'd prefer to go in the morning so I can sleep on the way. I think the overnight train is better because the scenery is amazing during the day. What do you suggest?
That's a great idea! The overnight sleeper carriages are comfortable. You can relax and enjoy the sunrise over the mountains. Have you booked your ticket yet?
Not yet. I was thinking of buying one from London to make sure I get a seat. It's cheaper there, right?

Oh, interesting! Well, tickets for the train are usually sold through the official railway website or at the station in Xi'an or Lanzhou. Prices vary depending on the season, but booking early is wise. You know, the view from Lanzhou is stunning before you reach the plateau.
Ah, I see. So I should avoid buying from foreign sites. What about the altitude sickness? Is it serious on this trip?

Yes, altitude sickness is a real concern because Lhasa is very high. Many people feel dizzy or tired at first. Actually, it helps to drink plenty of water and not exercise too hard for the first couple of days. Have you taken any medicine before?
No, I haven't. Should I buy some tablets in a pharmacy in Chengdu before I board?

That's a smart move. Pharmacies in Chengdu or even Xi'an have the right medicine. Also, bringing some dry food like rice cakes or noodles is good because they don't need much chewing. What else are you planning to pack?
I'll bring a warm jacket and a camera. Do you think I can stop in Xining to see something?

Absolutely! Xining is a lovely stop. You can visit the Qinghai Lake or the hot springs nearby. It's a good place to rest before the train continues. By the way, the food there is delicious; you must try the local mutton noodles.
Mutton noodles sound perfect. I really like trying new things. How much do the tickets cost?

The prices depend on the type of seat. A soft sleeper might cost around 1,200 yuan, while a hard seat is cheaper, about 500 yuan. Since it's a long trip, the sleeper is worth the extra money for comfort. Have you decided which one to choose?
I think I'll get the soft sleeper. It seems safer and more comfortable for such a long ride. Thanks for your help!
You're welcome! The train is indeed safer and cozier. You can sleep well and wake up in Lhasa with fresh air. If you need any more info, just ask. Safe travels!

messages.content: Hello Mr. Zhang! I'm Jing Hua. I'm here to buy some tea leaves as souvenirs. Have you been selling tea for long?
Hello Jing Hua! Yes, I've been here on this Old Street for twenty years. Actually, since 2004, I've been roasting my own tea leaves every day. Do you like green tea or oolong?
I like green tea because it's fresh. But I want to pack it nicely for my friends in Beijing. Do you have boxes like Starbucks?

Oh, interesting! Well, we have many beautiful boxes here too, Jing Hua. You know, these bamboo boxes are very popular for gifts. They are traditional and sturdy. Would you like to see a red lacquer box?
Yes, please show me that red one. It looks very nice. How much is it?
That's a good choice! To be honest, it's a bit expensive, but it's worth it. Usually, it's around 120 yuan. If you buy two, I can give you a small discount.
Okay, let's try two then. But can we make it 90 yuan each? I need to save money for my trip to Chongqing next month.
Well, 90 yuan is a bit low for this quality. Actually, I can give you a special price of 100 yuan each if you take them today. What do you think?
That sounds fair! I guess I'll take it. Do you also sell tea in small bags? My cousin in Xi'an likes tea very much.
Yes, we do! In fact, since last year, I've started selling loose tea in little paper bags for people like your cousin. They are cheaper and easier to carry. Would you like to try a small one first?
Great idea! I'll try one small bag. Is it from Hangzhou or another place?
This one is from the Longjing area near West Lake. It's famous because the water there is very soft. It makes the tea taste sweeter. Your cousin will love it!
I'm sure he will. Thank you, Mr. Zhang. You are very helpful. I will come back next spring to see you again.
You're welcome, Jing Hua! Come back anytime. Spring is the best time to drink fresh tea. Enjoy your trip to Chongqing and Xi'an!

messages.content: Hello, Lao Zhang! I'm Jing Hua. I've been coming to your shop since last year. The tea here is really good, isn't it?
Hi Jing Hua! It's been a pleasure having you here. Well, yes, our Longjing tea is famous. Many people come from all over China to taste it. Have you brought a friend today?
Actually, I didn't bring anyone, but I need to buy some gifts for my colleagues. You know, in my office, John is my boss and he loves Chinese culture.
Oh, interesting! So you want to buy tea for your boss? That's very thoughtful. I think your boss would appreciate the quality. Do you need any boxes to pack the tea nicely?
Yes, please! I want the red gift boxes. They look nice for sending by post. By the way, how much is this box of tea?
Sure, here are the red boxes. They are perfect for gifting. As for the price, it's 120 yuan for this pack. Although it's a bit more than usual, the quality is top-notch.
Okay, 120 yuan is a bit high for me. Can you give me a discount? I've been buying from you for a long time, after all.
Well, since you are a regular customer, I can offer you a small discount. How about 110 yuan? That's 10 yuan off. What do you think?
That sounds reasonable! I'll take two boxes then. But actually, I also want to ask about the price of the tea leaves in the loose form.
Good idea! The loose tea is cheaper per gram. It's 40 yuan for 50 grams. If you buy in bulk, the price might drop a bit more. Do you want to try a small sample first?
Sure, I'd love to try a sample. I want to make sure the taste is right before I decide. In addition, can you wrap the two boxes for me?
Of course! I'll wrap them in red paper with your name. It's my job to make sure your gifts look great. Here you go, two boxes of Longjing tea. Enjoy your afternoon!

messages.content: Hey Lin, have you tried that new noodle shop near the Li River yet? I heard the soup is amazing.
Wow, really? Well, I actually just went there yesterday and it was delicious! The beef noodles are my favorite. What kind of noodles do you like?
I like the spicy ones. But honestly, sometimes I miss a hot dog from home. It's just so convenient to grab one on the way.

Oh, interesting! Actually, here we have street vendors selling hot dogs too, but the local version is often filled with different ingredients. Have you tried the roasted pork skewers nearby? They are super tasty!
Yeah, I've heard of them. But the hot dogs are cheaper. I'm on a tight budget this month since I started my new job.
That makes sense. Well, prices here vary a lot. For example, the steamed buns are very affordable and filling. I think you should try making a meal with them and some soup.
Good idea. By the way, where is the best place to buy cheap snacks in this city?
You know, the night market near Wanshou Road is great! There are so many stalls selling fruits and snacks. It's crowded, but you can find good deals there.
Perfect. I guess I'll go there tomorrow evening. Do you know if it's open late?
Yes, it usually stays open until midnight. In fact, many locals go there after work to relax. You can also buy fresh fruit like lychees and oranges there.
Sounds like a plan. Thanks for the tip, I'll definitely check it out.
No problem! I hope you enjoy your meal. Let me know how the night market is, maybe we can go together next time.
Sure, that would be great. See you later!

messages.content: Hello! I'm Wei. It's really humid this morning. Do you like this kind of weather in the mountains?
Hi Wei! Yes, I like it. Actually, the mist looks very beautiful on Mount Qingcheng. The air is fresh, although it feels a bit damp.
I see. It reminds me of the fog in London sometimes. Do you think we should wait for the rain to stop before we start the hike?
That's a good question. Well, the rain might stop later. If we wait too long, the path could be slippery. But if the rain stops in ten minutes, we can go up to the panda sanctuary.
Okay, let's wait a bit. Have you hiked here since you started working as a guide?
Yes, I've been guiding here for three years. Since I started, I've walked this trail many times. It's tiring but fun, especially in the morning.
That sounds interesting. I guess I've never hiked in Sichuan before. The humidity here is much higher than in Beijing, right?
Exactly! To be honest, Beijing is much drier. Here in Chengdu and the mountains, it's always wet and cloudy. The humidity makes the tea taste better though.
Oh, I love tea. Do you have any recommendations? I prefer something strong, not too sweet.
Great choice! I recommend Longjing tea. It's not too sweet and has a clear taste. You know, many tourists buy it as a gift when they visit our village.
Nice! Maybe I'll buy some after the hike. By the way, I usually drink coffee from Starbucks in the city, but tea is better here.
Oh, interesting! Well, we have our own special tea that is very popular. People often drink it with a bowl of tofu puffs for breakfast. It's a healthy start for the day.
Tofu puffs? I've heard of that. Is it hard to find if I don't speak Chinese well?
Not at all! You can just point at the pictures. In fact, our village has English signs now. Also, the local food like mapo tofu is spicy but delicious.
Spicy? That sounds exciting. If I can handle the heat, I will try it. Have you ever visited other places like Xiamen or Guilin?
Yes, I went to Guilin once. The karst mountains there are amazing. Although, I prefer the quiet mountains here in Sichuan. Do you want to see the waterfall now?
Yes, please! The mist is beautiful. If the weather changes, we can go back to the village and eat some hot pot instead.
That's a great plan! Hot pot is warm and perfect for rainy days. We can eat it at the small restaurant near my home. Would you like to join me later?

messages.content: Hello! I'm Wei, and I've been visiting this mountain village near Mount Qingcheng since morning. The mist is so thick today. Have you seen the weather like this before?
Hi Wei! Yes, I have. Actually, it's very common in the rainy season here. The mist often covers the whole forest, making it feel like a dream. It's different from the dry air in Chengdu.
That sounds magical. I used to live in London when I was a child, so I know what heavy rain is like. But this humidity is different. It feels heavier.

Oh, interesting! That's a good comparison. In fact, the humidity in Sichuan can be quite sticky, especially in villages like this one. I think many people here prefer the breeze from the mountain streams instead.
True. If the rain stops, I want to hike up to the temple. Do you think the path will be safe then?

Well, it depends on how long the rain lasts. Actually, if the clouds clear by noon, the path to the main temple is usually safe. However, if it keeps raining, the stones might be too slippery for hiking.
I guess I'll wait and see. By the way, have you tried the local tea here? It's very good.
Yes, of course! The tea from here is famous. In fact, many tourists come just for it. It's a bit bitter at first, but then you taste the sweet aftertaste. Have you had any?
Not yet, but I will. Maybe I'll buy some to take back to my hometown in Beijing.
That's a great idea! Actually, it's a popular gift for friends in Beijing. By the way, the village has a small market near the entrance. You can buy fresh bamboo shoots there too.
Bamboo shoots? I've never eaten them before. They must be tasty!
They are delicious, especially if you stir-fry them with garlic. In fact, it's a traditional dish here. Would you like to try some later if the weather clears up?
Yes, please! I'd love to. Thank you for guiding me.
My pleasure! Well, let's just wait a bit more. If the rain stops soon, we can head to the temple. Otherwise, we can relax here for a while.

Oh, Xuanwu Lake is beautiful. I've been there many times. But to be honest, sometimes I feel tired after cleaning up. Do you think it's worth continuing?

I completely understand that feeling. Although it can be tiring, the sense of achievement is really great. For example, last week we planted some flowers, and now they're blooming beautifully. In addition, people in the neighborhood are very grateful.

Yes, my mom taught me how to do it. Last year, we made too many, so we gave them to our neighbors. By the way, sometimes I think about trying a hot dog after the event. It would be a nice change.
Oh, interesting! Well, our local street food vendors have some really delicious skewers and tangyuan instead. You could try those, they're quite popular among young people nowadays.
Skewers and tangyuan sound good. I've never had tangyuan before, but I heard the sweet soup is very comforting. Do you have a favorite neighborhood for events?

Actually, the old neighborhood in Qinhuai is amazing. We often hold cultural performances there. Since the buildings are historic, it adds a lot of charm to the gatherings. Have you visited the Confucius Temple nearby?
I have been there twice. The architecture is impressive. I guess if I help organize an event there, it would be meaningful for the community.

That's a great idea, Ling. If you help with the logistics, the event might run much smoother. To be honest, we always need more volunteers who understand the local culture well. Would you consider joining our planning team?

messages.content: Hello! I'm Liu Fang. It's a beautiful morning here at Stone Forest Park. I've been coming here since I retired. The air is so fresh.
Hello, Liu Fang! Yes, the morning air is wonderful here. I'm a volunteer ranger, and I love sharing this place with you. How long have you been hiking in nature?
About ten years now. I usually bring my own water bottle because tap water isn't always available on the trails. Do you recommend bringing much water?

Well, you're right about the water. In summer, it's very hot, so I always suggest carrying at least two liters. You know, there are some natural springs nearby, but it's safer to carry your own supply.
That's a good point. By the way, after the hike, I often go to a Starbucks nearby to relax and have a coffee.
Oh, interesting! Many people like to rest after hiking. Actually, there are also some local tea houses nearby where you can try our famous Dianhong tea. It's very refreshing too.
Dianhong tea sounds nice. Have you tried it? I think it pairs well with the mountain views.
Yes, I have! I've been drinking it for years. In fact, last year I drank it every day while watching the clouds move over the mountains. It's a special experience.
Wow, that sounds amazing. Do you think I should bring a jacket if the weather changes suddenly?
Absolutely, you should. The mountain weather is unpredictable. If it starts raining, the temperature drops quickly. You never know what might happen on the trail.
I guess I'll pack one just in case. Are there any specific trails you recommend for beginners like me?
Yes, the path to Shidi Village is perfect. It's not too steep, and you can see many different plants along the way. It's a great place to start.
Shidi Village sounds lovely. I'll definitely add that to my list. Thank you for your advice, ranger!
You're welcome! It's always a joy to help. Safe hiking, and see you on the trail again soon!

messages.content: Hi, I'm Liu Fang. It's been a while since I last came to this park. The morning air is so fresh!
Hello, Ms. Fang! Welcome back. Yes, the weather has been perfect since last week. I've seen many students visiting the trails near the lake.
That's true. I remember when I was a teacher, I used to take my students here for field trips. The mountains in the distance look very beautiful today.
They certainly do! In fact, if you look closely at the ridge, you might spot some golden monkeys climbing the trees. Have you ever tried to spot them before?
Oh, I have! Well, actually, I once saw a guide named John who was very helpful. He told me where the best spots were.
That's great! Well, guides here are very friendly too. My colleague, Xiao Ming, is excellent at finding wildlife. He knows exactly where the monkeys like to hide.
Really? Xiao Ming sounds like a good guide. I should ask him for advice next time. What do you usually pack for a hike?
Well, I usually carry a small backpack with some water and snacks. Since it's summer, it's important to stay hydrated. Do you usually drink water while hiking?
Yes, I always carry a bottle. In fact, I've been drinking a lot of water since I started coming here regularly.
That's a good habit! Actually, the springs in this park provide very clean water, but bringing your own bottle is safer. What kind of shoes do you wear?
I wear comfortable running shoes. Although they are not professional hiking boots, they work fine for flat paths.
That sounds reasonable. However, if you plan to go up the steep trail later, you might want something with better grip. What if you decide to climb the high peak next month?
That is a great idea. I think I will save some money to buy better boots. Thanks for your help, Xiao Ming!
You're welcome, Ms. Fang! Enjoy the rest of your walk. If you need any maps, just ask me or the other volunteers around here.

messages.content: Hi Dr. Liu, I'm Ming Wei from Nanjing. I've been feeling really tired since last week. Actually, I work at an office in the Xuanwu Lake area and I sit there for eight hours every day. It's hard for me to stand up and move around.

Hello Ming! Well, sitting for so long can make you feel very tired. To be honest, many people in Nanjing have the same problem because of long work hours. Have you been drinking enough water since you started feeling this way?
Yes, I try to drink water, but sometimes I just want to eat something heavy. Like, I really miss eating a big hot dog from a fast food place after work.

Oh, interesting! Well, hot dogs are tasty, but I think you should try a local bun called mantou instead. It's softer and easier to digest. By the way, do you eat lunch at the cafeteria near your office or do you go out?
I usually go to a small noodle shop on Jiangning Road. I love their soup, but the doctor says I should eat less oil. If I don't eat oil, will I get weak?

That's a good question. Actually, you don't need to stop oil completely, just eat less of it. For example, you can ask for soup without too much meat or oil. If you do this, you might feel better soon.
Okay, I will try that. What about the medicine? Do I need to buy pills or just change my diet? I guess I don't know which one is better for me.

Well, I think a small change in diet is better first. You know, medicine takes time to work, but fresh food helps immediately. If you keep eating healthy food for a few weeks, you might not need medicine at all.
That sounds nice. Can I get a prescription for vitamins then? I saw a pharmacy in the city that sells very good vitamins. I want to make sure I'm getting enough nutrients.

Sure, you can get vitamins here at the hospital. They have many kinds that are safe for everyone. I guess you should choose the ones with less sugar. Would you like me to write a prescription for you now?
Yes, please write it. Also, my mom says she always takes herbal tea from Hangzhou. Is that good for me too, or should I stick to western medicine like in the US?

Oh, herbal tea from Hangzhou is very famous and good! Actually, in China, many people prefer natural tea over western medicine. You can drink that, but try to avoid very strong medicine first. It's important to listen to your body.
Thank you, Dr. Liu. I feel a bit better already. I will drink the tea and eat less oil. See you next week?
You're welcome, Ming! Yes, see you next week. I hope you feel much stronger by then. Remember to take some walks in the park near Xuanwu Lake if you can. Take care!

Not really. My sleep is bad because the noise outside is loud. I usually stay up late watching videos on my phone until midnight.

That explains it. I've seen many patients whose sleep quality has gone down since they use phones late at night. Maybe you should try to put the phone away an hour earlier. What time do you usually go to bed?
Usually around 12:30 AM. But sometimes I go to a Starbucks in the city center to drink coffee and work even later.

Yes, I have some green tea. But I think I need to check my blood pressure because I feel dizzy sometimes.

No, I haven't. I only felt dizzy when I was running upstairs quickly.

Sure, that would be great. How long does the whole process usually take?

Okay, I understand. I'll wait here while you prepare the forms. Please tell me if I need to fill anything out first.

Thank you, Doctor. I'll take some water. I hope my blood pressure is not too high.

messages.content: Hi! I'm Wei Ming. It's early autumn in Chengdu, isn't it? The air feels so fresh. I've been thinking about improving my health naturally. Do you like drinking herbal tea?

Hello, Wei Ming! Yes, it's definitely fresh here. Actually, I love herbal tea myself. Since last spring, I've been drinking Goji Berry tea every morning. It helps me stay energetic. Have you tried it before?
I have tried it, but I usually drink coffee instead. I think it gives me more energy in the morning. Maybe I should switch to tea eventually.

That's true, coffee is very popular. However, if you switch to tea, your stomach will feel much better. You know, I've felt a bit of heartburn since I started drinking coffee again last month. Would you like to try a pot with me?
Sure, that sounds nice. By the way, I often buy my coffee beans at Starbucks downtown. It's quite convenient.

Oh, interesting! Well, there are many good tea shops in the Wuhua area too. Actually, you could visit the old shop near Jiuheyuan Street. The owner makes excellent Pu'er tea that has been stored for years.
Jiuheyuan sounds great. Do you think acupuncture is good for back pain? I've had some issues lately.

Absolutely! In fact, many people here use acupuncture for back problems. I had some lower back pain a few weeks ago, and I've been going to a clinic near Minfeng Road ever since. It's been very effective.
That's good to hear. Do you think diet is more important than exercise for health?

Well, honestly, both are important. Although exercise is necessary, a balanced diet is the foundation. For example, if you eat too much spicy food like Mapo Tofu, it might hurt your stomach even if you exercise every day. What do you think?
I guess you're right. I try to eat less meat and more vegetables. Do you have any advice for a healthy breakfast?

Yes, of course! A bowl of congee with some shredded pork and green onions is perfect. Additionally, you can add some pickled vegetables to it. It's warm and easy to digest. I usually eat this since 7 am every day.
That sounds very comforting. Maybe I will try making it at home next week. Thanks for the advice, friend!
You are welcome, Wei Ming! If you have any questions about TCM or diet, just ask me. Actually, we can go to that tea shop together later this afternoon. It will be great!

messages.content: Hi Ma Lin! I've been practicing calligraphy since last month, and I really want to improve my skills. How long have you been teaching this?

Hello Sun Lei! It's great to see you here on a Saturday morning. I've been teaching at this community center in Xiguan for over ten years now. Actually, I remember when I first started, I used to struggle with the brush strokes too.
That's encouraging! I find that using special rice paper is important for the ink to flow properly. Do you think I should buy a brand like Starbucks to get better pens?

Oh, I see! Well, getting good pens is definitely important. But in China, we usually prefer traditional bamboo brushes rather than imported ones. For example, the 'Moyu' brand makes excellent brushes that are very popular here. Have you tried using rice paper before?
Yes, I have! The texture is amazing. Although it's a bit harder to control at first, I think it helps me focus more. What do you do when you finish a piece?

That's wonderful! Many students feel the same way. When I finish a piece, I usually let it dry for a while and then hang it up on the wall in the studio. To be honest, I also like to frame them in simple wooden frames so they look nice in the living room later.
Framing is a great idea. I'm thinking of displaying some of my work on my balcony this summer. Do people often visit your class?

Yes, many people do! Most of our students live nearby in neighborhoods like Baiyun or Huangpu. They often come after work on weekdays, but weekends are busier because families like to practice together. Would you like to bring a friend next time?
Maybe I will! I have a cousin who lives in Shenzhen and he's interested in art too. If he comes, will we need to book ahead?

I think it would be best to book ahead, especially since we're getting more popular. We have a class at 10 AM and another at 2 PM, so there might be few spots left. Actually, if you book by Friday, we usually can save a spot for you.
Perfect, I'll call you next week then. Do you have any tips for keeping the brushes clean?

Of course! After each session, just rinse the brush with warm water and gently squeeze it out. Never let it dry out, because that can ruin the hair. Also, keep them in a case when you're not using them. It's simple, but it really helps.
Thanks for the advice! I'll make sure to do that. Looking forward to seeing you again soon.
You're welcome, Sun Lei! See you next week. Have a nice weekend practicing in the meantime!

I guess I should try it soon. Maybe I can bring some to my office next week.

Yes, but sometimes I feel like I need a change. Maybe something lighter, like a person named John from America would choose, or maybe a French coffee style?

Oh, interesting! I see. Actually, some people here prefer lighter tea like Green tea from Hangzhou or Jasmine tea from Fuzhou. They are very popular too. If you want something different, we have some high-quality white tea that is very delicate.
White tea sounds nice. I haven't had white tea since I moved here. How do you brew it?

That's great, you're learning fast! To be honest, white tea needs less hot water than other types. You should use water around 80 degrees, not boiling. Also, don't put the leaves in too much; a little goes a long way.
Got it, less hot water and fewer leaves. Do you sell the leaves in small bags or bulk?
We sell both! If you want to try first, I can give you a small bag of the white tea. But if you know what you like, buying from our bulk section is cheaper. You get better quality there.
I think I'll try the small bag first. What about the water? Where can I get good water in Guangzhou?
Good question! Well, many people here use filtered water or buy bottled mineral water from local brands. Actually, using tap water directly is not recommended for tea because it might taste strange.
I see. So I should buy a filter. Does your shop sell water filters?
No, we don't sell filters, but you can find them in any electronics market in Tianhe District. Or, you can just use our bottled water for brewing. It's free with your purchase today!
That's very kind of you. I'll take the white tea then. Thank you for the advice.
You're welcome! I'm sure you'll enjoy the taste. By the way, if you visit Xishui Village next time, they make excellent tea there. It's a bit far, but the scenery is beautiful. Enjoy your tea!

messages.content: Hi Qiang, I'm so excited! I finally bought an old apartment in Tang Paradise Community. It's got such history.
That's great news, Xiao Fang! Well, living in Tang Paradise is really special because of the old Tang Dynasty style. Have you started thinking about what furniture you need?
Yes, I have been looking at some nice sofas. Actually, I saw a very cool leather one that reminds me of the style I love in New York apartments.
Oh, interesting! Well, leather furniture is nice, but for an old house here, I think a wooden sofa with soft cushions would fit the vibe better. What do you think?
I guess you're right about the wood. But I'm also worried about the noise. The neighbors are doing heavy construction since last week.
That sounds stressful! You know, construction noise is common in this area, but it usually stops by the afternoon. Have you checked if they have a quiet time agreement?
I've tried to talk to them, but they say they have to finish by Friday. It's really loud when they use the jackhammer.
I see. Well, maybe you can get some good noise-canceling headphones or play some soft classical music on your phone to relax. Do you have a favorite musician?
Actually, I love listening to the local radio station. It plays folk songs from Shaanxi. Besides, I'm checking the safety standards too.
That's a smart idea. Safety is very important, especially with old buildings. Did you check the electrical wiring and the roof structure yet?
Yes, I did. The electrician said everything is safe, but the roof might need some repair. He said he will come next week.
Good, that's a relief. In addition, make sure he uses high-quality materials. Would you like me to recommend some reliable workers from my list?
That would be helpful. To be honest, I'm a bit tired of all these decisions, but I want the house to be perfect.
I understand completely. Renovating an old home can be tiring, but it's worth it. You've got this. Let's take it one step at a time, okay?
Thank you, Qiang. I feel much better now. Let's meet again next week to discuss the roof repairs.

messages.content: Hi Qiang Li! I'm Xiao Fang. I just bought an old apartment in Tang Paradise Community in Xi'an, and I need your advice.
Hello Xiao Fang! That's great news. Tang Paradise is such a historic place. Actually, renovating an old building there can be tricky because of the old walls.
Yes, exactly. I want to keep the old wooden beams, but I also want to install modern air conditioning. I've been thinking about it for weeks since I moved in.
That makes sense. Installing split units without ruining the beams is a challenge. By the way, have you checked the safety standards for the electrical wiring yet?
Not really. I'm worried about the noise from the construction nearby in Chang'an District. It's been going on for hours yesterday, so I could hardly sleep last night.
Oh, construction noise is really annoying. I guess you might need some thick curtains or special soundproofing windows. Well, it's better to check the noise levels before you finish the renovation.
Good point. I also love the idea of having a big open kitchen. Maybe I can put a gas stove there, just like my friend Mary does in her house in London.
An open kitchen sounds nice for cooking! In China, many people prefer separate rooms, but it depends on the space. If you choose a good range hood, the smell won't be a problem.
True. I think I'll hire a professional team from a company in Shaanxi. Do you have any recommendations for reliable workers?
Actually, I work with several local teams who know the old buildings well. For example, there is a good group in the north part of Xi'an who specialize in historic homes.
That sounds perfect. I want to make sure the floor doesn't crack when I put heavy furniture in the living room. I've heard that new tiles are stronger.
Yes, modern tiles are much stronger than the old ones. However, you have to be careful when laying them on the old foundation. I suggest checking the ground first.
Okay, I will do that. Thank you, Qiang Li. I feel much more confident now about fixing up this place.
You're welcome, Xiao Fang. Take your time, and don't rush the process. If you have more questions later, just ask me. Good luck with your project!

messages.content: Hi Xu Qing! I'm Chen Yang. I've been looking for a summer internship since last month. Do you have any advice?
Hello Chen! Of course, I'd be happy to help. Actually, many juniors are looking around now because the summer starts soon. Have you decided where to apply yet?
Not really. I was thinking of applying to a big company in Shanghai. Maybe one of those famous international brands like McDonald's would be good for my resume.

Oh, interesting! Well, big companies here are always popular, but did you know there are many excellent local tech firms in Zhongguancun or even in Shenzhen now? I think they offer great training too.
Really? I didn't know that. I guess I should focus on local companies. What do you think about the interview process there?

You're right! Actually, local interviews often focus more on practical skills and group discussions. For example, they might give you a case study to solve in a team. Are you good at working in groups?
Yes, I've worked in several projects. But I'm a bit nervous about the English part. Should I prepare specific phrases?
Don't worry too much. Most interviews are in Chinese, so just be confident. By the way, practicing with a friend who is a senior student can really help you relax.
That sounds like a good idea. Do you know anyone? Maybe someone from my university in Hangzhou.

Hangzhou is a great place for internships! I know a few seniors from Zhejiang University. They are very helpful. You could ask your professors for recommendations too. What about your English speaking skills?
I think I'm okay. I've been watching movies and listening to podcasts since last year. But I still make mistakes sometimes.
That's normal! Everyone makes mistakes. Actually, I've had the same problem when I started. The key is to keep practicing. Have you tried joining an English club at your school?
No, I haven't. I'll try it next week. Thanks for your advice, Xu Qing. I feel much better now.
You're welcome! Good luck with your applications. If you need more tips, feel free to ask. Remember, preparation is key, but confidence is also important.

Hey Chen Yang! Yes, I've already applied to a few tech firms in Pudong since last month. Actually, I'm thinking of visiting one tomorrow morning.
That sounds great! What kind of work do you usually prepare for an interview? Do you need to wear a suit?
Well, it depends on the company. In my experience, business casual is fine for most places. You don't need to wear a full suit unless it's a very formal bank.
Oh, I see. I usually meet my friend Mary after class to practice English together. She is very helpful.
Oh, interesting! Practicing with a partner is a good idea. In China, students often study in pairs or groups too. For example, we used to role-play interviews since last semester.
Really? What do you usually ask in the practice? Do you ask about salary first?
Actually, we usually start with self-introduction. We don't talk about money immediately because it's a bit too direct in Chinese culture. Maybe we can ask about projects first.

messages.content: Hey neighbor, it's a beautiful autumn day! I've been planning a hike near Jade Dragon Snow Mountain since yesterday. What do you think?
Well, that's a great idea! Actually, the weather has been perfect for hiking these days. The air is cool but not cold yet. Have you decided which trail you want to take?
I'm thinking of the Blue Moon Valley route. I heard it's scenic. But I need to pack some snacks. Maybe I'll bring a pizza from a chain store for lunch because it's easy to carry.

Oh, interesting! Well, carrying a sandwich or some buns would be much better since they don't get soggy in the wind. You know, there's a famous noodle shop near the entrance where you can buy hot soup if you get hungry. It's much more filling than dry food.
That sounds like a good plan. I guess I should check the weather forecast again just in case it rains. Do you know if the path gets slippery?

I think so, especially in the afternoon when the clouds cover the sun. You should definitely wear good shoes that grip well. Last time I went there, it was a bit wet, so I brought a raincoat just in case.
I definitely need better shoes. I've had a pair since last year, but they are worn out. Should I go to the sports store in the old town or just buy new ones online?

Actually, going to the shop in the old town is better because you can try them on first. Online shopping is convenient, but if they don't fit well, it's a hassle to return them. By the way, do you know how far the trail is roughly?
I think it's about five kilometers to the viewpoint and five back. So, round trip is ten kilometers. That's not too far for me.

That's a reasonable distance for a morning hike. Although, if you start late, you might rush at the end. It's always better to start early so you can enjoy the sunrise. Have you ever seen the sunrise there?
No, I haven't yet. I've only been to the valley floor. I want to see the snow mountain from above. It must be amazing.

It really is! The view from the higher peak is breathtaking. I remember taking a photo there once, and it was so clear. You should go soon, especially this time of year. The colors of the leaves are fantastic.
I really want to go this weekend. Let's meet at the entrance at 7 AM. I'll bring my water bottle and the snacks we talked about.
Sounds perfect! I'll see you there at 7. Don't forget to bring your camera too. It's going to be a lovely day out.

messages.content: Hi! I've been planning a weekend hike near Lijiang since last week. Do you think the weather will be good on Saturday?
Well, actually, it's been sunny in Lijiang for most of the autumn season. I guess the mountain air is cool but clear. Have you checked the forecast for Jade Dragon Snow Mountain?
Yes, I looked at it this morning. If it rains, I might stay in the city. But if the sky is blue, I'll go to the trailhead early. It's the perfect time of year.
That's a smart plan. You know, the trails get crowded quickly after 9 am. To be honest, I prefer starting before the morning rush. Which path are you thinking of taking?
I want to try the old route to Baisha. It's quieter and has nice views. But I need to pack more water than usual because the path is long.
Oh, interesting! Baisha is a great choice for a peaceful walk. By the way, have you tried hiking the path near Yuhu Village? It's less steep and has some nice bamboo groves along the way.
I've heard of Yuhu! I think I'll go there instead. What should I bring for lunch? I usually eat a sandwich at the picnic spot.
Well, sandwiches are fine, but you know, many hikers prefer fresh noodles or dumplings from a local stall near the trail. There's a small shop just before the river crossing.
That sounds delicious! I've never had noodles while walking. Do you think it's easy to find hot food at high altitude? I'm not sure I can eat spicy things.
Actually, the shops usually have mild broth options too. In addition, many places serve warm rice porridge which is very comforting in the cold mountain air.
Perfect. I'll add rice porridge to my list. When did you start hiking in Lijiang? I've only done it a few times.
I've been coming here since I moved to Yunnan three years ago. At first, I was scared of the high mountains, but now I love the views. You should try the sunrise spot on the peak next month.
